with the following prayer:-

4. Aforementioned application was disposed of finally by this Court, vide order dated 23.08.2023.

For ready reference, the order dated 23.08.2023 is reproduced herein below:-
"1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants to quash the charge-sheet No.70 of 2021 dated 12.08.2021, cognizance order dated 01.02.2022 and entire proceedings of case No.3050 of 2022 (State Vs. Mohit and others) arising out of case crime No.101 of 2020, under Sections 498-A, 323, 452,
504 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station-Mahila, District-Moradabad,
which is pending in the court of Civil Judge, Jr.Division, F.T.C..
3.

entities.text: case No.3050 of 2022 (State Vs. Mohit and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the parties have reconciled their differences and a compromise has been entered between them, copy of compromise deed dated 09.05.2023 has been annexed as Annexure 3 to this affidavit.

Therefore,
no useful purpose would be served in continuing the proceedings before the Court below and the same is not only sheer wastage of time of the Court but also abuse of process of law.

4. Learned A.G.A., however, submits that it is the concerned court below, which has to verify the fact as to whether the parties have entered into compromise, hence the applicants may approach the concerned court below and move an application with respect to compromise between the parties, which will be decided in accordance with law.

5. In view of above, without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, both the parties are directed to appear before the Court below along with compromise deed as well certified copy of this order within two weeks from today.

It is expected that Court below may fix a date for the verification of the compromise and after ensuring the presence of the parties, pass an appropriate order with respect to the same in accordance with law, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of two months from the date of production of a certified copy of this order, if there is no Mohit Kumar And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148437940/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: other legal impediment.

While passing the order verifying the compromise, the Court concerned shall also record the statements of the parties as to whether all the terms and conditions mentioned in the original compromise deed, so filed, have been fulfilled or not?

6. The Court in that scenario will allow the parties to obtain certified copy of the report as well as compromise and it will be open to the applicants to approach this Court again for quashing of the proceedings.
7. For a period of two months, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case.
8. With the aforesaid directions, this application is finally disposed off."

5. Since the directions contained in paragraph 5 of aforementioned order could not be complied with by the parties within the time period fixed by this Court, therefore, this time extension application has been filed by applicants seeking further time to comply with the same.

6. Learned counsel for applicants contends that the parties had already approached the Family Court, Moradabad by way of Matrimonial Petition No. 166 of 2023 (Smt. Radha Vs. Mohit Kumar),
under Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act i.e. Divorce by way of mutual consent.

entities.text: Matrimonial Petition No. 166 of 2023 (Smt. Radha Vs. Mohit Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aforesaid matrimonial petition was decreed by Court below, vide judgment and decree dated 04.09.2024.

He,
therefore, submits that in view of above, no useful purpose shall be served in prolonging the criminal prosecution of applicants in aforementioned criminal case.

Reference has further been made to the judgment of Supreme Court in Shlok Bhardwaj V. Runika Bhardwaj (2015) 2 SCC 721,
wherein Apex Court has held that compromise in matrimonial matters should be treated as an effective compromise so as to bring all dispute between the parties to an end.

entities.text: Shlok Bhardwaj V. Runika Bhardwaj (2015) 2 SCC 721
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He, therefore, submits that in view of above, equity demands that one more opportunity be granted to the applicants to comply with the directions contained in aforementioned order.
7. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. representing State-opposite party-1 has no objection to the prayer made by the learned counsel for applicants.

8. Having heard the learned counsel for applicants, the learned A.G.A. for State and upon perusal of record, this Court finds that in view of the judgment and decree dated 04.09.2024 passed by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Moradabad, whereby a decree of divorce on the basis of mutual consent has been passed by Court and also the law laid down by the Apex Court in Shlok Bhardwaj (Supra), interest of justice shall be served, in case, applicants are granted one more opportunity to comply with the directions contained in paragraph 5 of the order dated 23.08.2023.
9. In view of above, this time extension application is liable to be allowed.
10. It is, accordingly, allowed.
